description: Bottom-up normalization discriminator: three levels deep, all removed. {a:{b:{c:null}}} → {} bottom-up (correct) vs {a:{b:{}}} with a naive top-down single-pass. The bottom-up pass removes c:null (level 3), which makes b={} empty (level 2), which makes a={} empty (level 1), which is then removed at the top level. A top-down pass stops at level 1 because {b:{c:null}} is not null/empty at the time it is examined, and never revisits a once b becomes empty. This vector is the §0 (survived-falsification) discriminator confirming normalize() is genuinely bottom-up.
mutation_probe: Removing the recursion from normalize() (making it process only the top level) would produce {"a":{"b":{}}} (digest differs from the pinned value above). The test fails if normalize() is replaced with a single-level filter.
note: The digest 44136fa3... is the SHA-256 of the two bytes 0x7B 0x7D ('{}' in UTF-8). Any implementation that produces a different digest has not applied absent-field normalization bottom-up across all three levels.
